analysis.investment_thesis: Affle has built a respectable mobile advertising technology platform with a 45% revenue CAGR over 7 years and — importantly — consistently positive free cash flow, which is rare in ad tech. However, the CPCU (cost-per-converted-user) model's moat is unclear in a world where Google, Meta, and Apple control the underlying inventory and data, and the company's serial acquisition of 5 platforms (Appnext, Mediasmart, Jampp, RevX, YouAppi) raises integration risk and obscures organic vs. inorganic returns.
key_strengths: Consistent FCF generation (positive every year FY2020-FY2025, reaching INR 266 Cr in FY2025) with nearly no debt (D/E 0.01) and INR 1,047 Cr cash — financial discipline is real
Revenue CAGR of 45.1% over 7 years with operating margin expansion from 27% to 21% (still healthy) — demonstrated ability to scale the business model
Strong promoter holding (54.92%) with significant FII/DII participation (34.5% combined) — market confidence with aligned founder incentives
key_risks: ROCE of 16.8% and ROE of 14% are mediocre for a business growing at 45% — serial acquisitions have diluted per-rupee returns substantially; equity base grew from INR 230 Cr to INR 3,256 Cr in 5 years largely through capital raises
Existential platform risk: Apple's App Tracking Transparency (ATT) and Google's deprecation of third-party cookies directly threaten the targeting capabilities that underpin the CPCU model
Operating margin compressed from ~27% (FY2021) to 21.3% (FY2025) even during a high-growth phase — suggests mix shift toward lower-margin geographies or competitive pricing pressure
red_flags: Five major acquisitions (Appnext, Mediasmart, Jampp, RevX, YouAppi) in roughly 5 years — serial acquirers rarely compound capital as well as organic growers; goodwill/intangibles risk
Total assets grew 9.7x from INR 402 Cr to INR 3,914 Cr while net profit grew 5.8x from INR 66 Cr to INR 382 Cr — assets are growing faster than earnings, suggesting acquisition premium dilution
Other income of INR 94 Cr in FY2025 represents 25% of operating income — inflating headline profitability with what is likely treasury income on the large cash pile
analysis.detailed_analysis: Affle deserves credit for what it has built — a cash-generative, nearly debt-free mobile ad platform growing quickly in the right geography (India plus emerging markets) at the right time (smartphone penetration). The FCF track record is the most encouraging data point; most ad tech companies consume cash. But the 14% ROE on a business growing revenue at 45% is a troubling signal — each acquisition appears to be accreting revenue while diluting returns. The classic Munger test: does this business earn high returns on incremental capital without acquisitions? The evidence is ambiguous. At 47x P/E, you need both the growth to continue AND the returns on capital to improve — a demanding dual condition. I'd watch for margin expansion and acquisition discipline before committing meaningful capital.
